subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Digital Twins: Virtual Copies of Real Things
description: A fast breakdown of Digital Twins: Virtual Copies of Real Things for builders.

hook.text: A digital twin is a virtual replica of a physical object, updated in real time with sensor data. It predicts the future.

buildup.text: GE creates digital twins of jet engines. Sensors in the real engine feed data to the twin, which predicts wear and failures.

discovery.text: Singapore built a digital twin of the entire city. Traffic, weather, energy, and building data merge into one living model.

twist.text: Digital twins can simulate scenarios that would be too dangerous or expensive to test in reality. Crash tests become simulations.

climax.text: NASA used a digital twin to diagnose and fix problems on Apollo 13 from Earth. The concept is older than the name.

punchline.text: Build it twice. One real. One digital. The digital one warns you first.

quiz.question: How did NASA use the concept of a digital twin during Apollo 13?
options: They simulated re-entry angles using a virtual model of the damaged spacecraft
They diagnosed and fixed problems from Earth using a ground-based replica
They uploaded software patches to the spacecraft's onboard computer
